dashboard.label: MCP Server & Claude Desktop
dashboard.description: Connect Claude Desktop to this Splunk via the Splunk MCP Server — what to install and how to use it.

html.h2: Talk to Splunk from Claude Desktop (MCP)
html.p: The Splunk MCP Server app exposes Splunk to any MCP client (like Claude Desktop) over the management port. Once connected, you can ask Claude in plain language — "search errors in berlin_linux in the last hour", "list my indexes" — and it runs the search in Splunk and returns the results.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way to give an AI assistant tools. The Splunk app is the "server"; Claude Desktop is the "client".

panel.title: Status — is the MCP Server app installed?

search.query: | rest /services/apps/local | search title=* (title="*mcp*" OR label="*MCP*") | eval Status="installed" | table title label version Status

ol.li:
Install the app — done automatically by apply.sh when you supply your splunk.com credentials at the startup prompt ("Splunk.com username for Splunkbase downloads"). The table above should list the MCP app. If not, re-run apply.sh and enter your creds.
Getting HTTP 403? Splunkbase requires you to accept the app's license terms once in a browser before the API will serve it. Log in at splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7931, click Download, accept the terms (you can cancel the actual download), then re-run apply.sh — the download then succeeds for your account.
No entitlement issues but still stuck? You can also host the app .spl at a reachable URL and let apply.sh fetch it via SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS (see the ITSI Setup page — same mechanism).

Grant the MCP capability to the user/role that will connect. The simplest for a demo is to use admin (already has every capability). To use a lab user, add the app's capability (e.g. mcp_tool_execute) to their role under Settings → Roles.
Create an auth token for that user: Settings → Tokens (enable token authentication if prompted) → New Token → copy it. This is the bearer token Claude Desktop will use.
Point Claude Desktop at Splunk. Edit claude_desktop_config.json (Claude Desktop → Settings → Developer → Edit Config) and add the server via the mcp-remote proxy:

html.p: Save, fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop. The splunk tools then appear in Claude Desktop (look for the tools/plug icon).

ul.li: "Using Splunk, list the indexes I can access."
"Search index=berlin_linux for errors in the last hour and summarize."
"What sourcetypes are in london_metrics and how many events?"
"Run | tstats count by index, sourcetype and show me a table."

html.p: Claude runs these as searches through the MCP server and returns the results — RBAC still applies to whatever user's token you configured.

ul.li: Version: the MCP app is certified for Splunk 8.0–10.2; this lab is 10.4, so confirm it loads (the status table above). If it won't load, that's the reason.
TLS: the box uses a self-signed cert. If mcp-remote refuses it, allow insecure TLS in the app's mcp.conf ([mcp] ssl_verify = false) or trust the cert on the client.
Reachability: Claude Desktop must be able to reach 198.18.1.124:8089 (the management port).
Resets each session: the token and any role/capability change are runtime state — recreate them each session (the app install itself is automated).
